title: pricing back-of-envelope: tokens & tiers
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick personal scratchpad to capture token math, unit economics, and early tier ideas for hosted API pricing.
- NOT final. For internal discussion with product + finance.

High-level assumptions (very rough):
- Infrastructure cost per GPU-hour: $3.00 (amortized & including infra ops) for shared infra mix (varies by model/hw).
- Throughput: depends on model; use example numbers below.
- Average tokens generated per user request: 300 tokens (prompt + completion).
- Requests per month (active user): 1,000 calls (aggressive for power users) -> 300k tokens/month.
- Exchange rate: 1M tokens ~ X GPU-seconds depending on model; we'll approximate per-token cost.

Token cost back-of-envelope (example model categories):
1) Small Llama-ish (quantized):
   - Perf: ~3000 tokens/sec per GPU (batching + kv cache) -> 10M tokens/hour.
   - Cost per hour (amortized infra+ops): $3.00 -> cost/token = $3 / 10M = $0.0000003/token (~0.0003 cents/token).
   - Add overhead (storage, networking, SRE ops, margin) -> target cost to Redwood = $0.0000015/token (5x)

2) Medium (7B dense, higher perf):
   - Perf: 1500 tokens/sec -> 5.4M tokens/hour.
   - Raw cost/token = $3 / 5.4M = $0.00000056/token.  After overhead/margin ~ $0.000003/token.

3) Large (70B / LLMs with expensive kernels):
   - Perf: 150 tokens/sec -> 540k tokens/hour.
   - Raw cost/token = $3 / 540k = $0.0000056/token. After ops/margin -> $0.00002 - $0.00005/token.

Takeaway: per-token raw infra cost is extremely model-dependent (x100+ from small to huge). Pricing should reflect model class.

Simple unit-economics example (hosted API)
- Offer three model tiers mapped to cost buckets: small, medium, large.
- List price = cost_to_company * markup. Target gross margin 60%+ (depends on go-to-market).

Example list prices (starting point):
- Small-tier model: cost $0.0000015/token -> list $0.000004/token (rounded)
- Medium-tier model: cost $0.000003/token -> list $0.000009/token
- Large-tier model: cost $0.00003/token -> list $0.00009/token

Monthly customer example (SaaS product using medium-tier):
- Active users: 200 users, each 10k tokens/day -> 6M tokens/month total -> cost_to_redwood = 6M * $0.000003 = $18/month.
- List revenue = 6M * $0.000009 = $54/month -> gross margin ~67%.

Free tier and trial credits
- Free tier quotas should be mapped to token budgets (e.g., 50k tokens free / month) rather than calls. Easier to reason about model cost.
- Trial credits: give $50-$100 in tokens to play with; cost exposure depends on mix of heavy models. Use model caps for trials (e.g., trial only allows small/medium).

Committed / Dedicated pricing (Reserved capacity)
- Offer committed monthly baseline for Dedicated. Example: commit to N GPU-hours/month (or RU = reserved units) -> discounted per-token price vs hosted.
- Pricing structure: baseline committed $/hour + overage per token (or per-second). Equivalent to current reserved capacity market.

Tier ideas (hosted API):
- Free: 50k tokens/month, streaming disabled for large models, rate-limited
- Hobby: 5M tokens/month at $X (map to small/medium mix)
- Startup: 50M tokens/month incl. cheap embedding calls batch quota
- Growth: 200M tokens/month + priority support + per-route quotas
- Enterprise: custom (SLA + dedicated + VPC + billing terms)

Bundling + feature gating thoughts:
- Advanced features (rollouts, per-route tracing, long retention in Console) as paid add-ons or tied to tiers.
- Embeddings pricing separate (lower per-unit cost but charged per vector/usage).
- Rate limits + concurrency thresholds for hosted tiers.

Embeddings/unit math (quick):
- Embedding call cost heavily tied to model size but throughput per GPU is much larger because it's single forward pass (no autoregressive sampling).
- Example: 10k vectors/minute per GPU; amortized cost/token equivalent not useful. Instead price per 1k embeddings: e.g., $0.001 - $0.01 per 1k depending on model.

Other levers to reduce cost (and justify price parity):
- Auto-batching across tenants -> increases tokens/sec achievable -> reduces cost/token.
- Prefix/KV caching for assistant-like workloads -> reduces average tokens processed (cache hits).
- Quantized model variants and fallback chains: prefer small quantized models when policy allows.

Open questions / TODOs:
- More accurate infra costs by model and region (get raw GPU-hour cost + network + storage). TODO: ask infra for up-to-date amortized $/GPU-hour by instance type. (Ticket: PRJ-789)
- Understand typical token distribution per customer by segment (GTM). Data request to analytics.
- How to price streaming vs non-streaming? Do we charge per-token equally or premium for streaming?
- Embeddings: should we separate by vector dimension & model performance? likely yes.
- Need decision on free-tier token budget vs rate limits.

Quick notes for discussion with finance (what I will ask):
- Target gross margin by segment (self-serve vs enterprise).
- Acceptable payback window for CAC given pricing.
- Discounting matrix for committed capacity (1m-10m tokens -> X% off; >100M -> custom).

Rough next steps:
- Lock down infra $/GPU-hour per model class (infra team).
- Get token distribution histograms for product categories (analytics).
- Draft a price sheet mapping models -> token price with example customer bills.
- Iterate in product review + finance.

Random scratch lines:
- Maybe bundle embeddings as "20M embeddings/month" instead of tokens to simplify buyer math.
- Consider enterprise metric pricing (requests-per-second SLA + reserved concurrency) for ad platforms.
- Keep a "fallback" cheaper model for high-volume low-cost paths.

End of scratchpad (notes messy).
